summary: Sambhavi Ganesh studied at Lady Shri Ram College, Tata Institute of Social Sciences, and the University of Edinburgh under Radhika Govinda. An Indologist, she served at Kudumbashree National Resource Organisation (2019-2020) and King's College London (2025-2026).

Samiran Chandra Chakrabarti is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He held posts at the University of Calcutta and served as a Professor (Special Invitee) at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).

Sampadananda Mishra is a scholar in Indology and linguistics who studied at Pondicherry University. He served as Director at Rishihood University (2021) and as a Professor at Hindu University of America (2022).
Sampan Chakrabarty, a scholar in Indology, conducted doctoral research under Pallab Sengupta (attested 2026) and served as a Research Scholar/Fellow at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).

Samten Gyaltsen Karmay is a Tibetology and religious studies scholar. He studied at Drepung Monastery and the University of London under David Snellgrove, later holding posts at SOAS, CNRS, and serving as President of the IATS (1995-2000).

Samuel Beal was a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Trinity College, Cambridge and Durham University, and held posts including Professor of Chinese at University College London (1877) and at the University of London (~1877-1889).

Samuel Charles Hill was a historian and Indologist educated at University College London. He served in the Bengal Educational Service (1881-1912), taught at Dhaka College (1881), and held charge at the National Archives of India (1899-1912).
Samuel Charters Macpherson was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his studies at the University of Edinburgh (1822-1823) and Trinity College, Cambridge (~1823).

Samuel De Coster Atkins was an Indologist and linguist who earned his A.B. and Ph.D. at Princeton University. After working at Baylor University (1935-1937), he served as Assistant Professor of Classics and Sanskrit at Princeton (1937-1978).

Samuel George Frederick Brandon was a scholar of religious studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Leeds (~1930-1936) and held an academic post at the University of Manchester (~1951-1971).

Samuel Gottlieb Rudolf Henzi worked in religious studies, studying at Bern, Tübingen, Göttingen, and in Paris under Silvestre de Sacy and Chézy. In 1820, he became Professor of Exegesis and Oriental Languages at the University of Tartu.

Samuel Grant Oliphant was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Princeton and Johns Hopkins under Maurice Bloomfield, and held posts at Johns Hopkins, Grove City College (1911), and The University of Olivet (~1914-1919).
Samuel Heinrich Ribbach was a scholar in Tibetology. He served as a missionary with the Moravian Church (1892-1927) and held a post at the Museum am Rothenbaum.
Samuel Henry Butcher was educated at Marlborough College and Trinity College, Cambridge. He held academic posts at the University of Edinburgh (~1882-1903) and Harvard University (~1904).

Samuel Henry Kellogg was an Indologist and linguist educated at Princeton University and Princeton Theological Seminary. He taught at Allahabad Theological Training School (1873-1876) and was Professor of Systematic Theology at Pittsburgh Theological Seminary (1877-1885).
Samuel Johnson was a scholar in linguistics. He completed his education at King Edward VI School, King Edward VI College, Stourbridge (~1725-1726), and Pembroke College, Oxford (1728-1731).

Samuel M. Grupper is a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He earned his PhD at Indiana University Bloomington, studying under Irving Yucheng Lo and Philip West.
Samuel Mateer was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He studied at Bedford Theological College (~1856-1858) and served as a missionary with the London Missionary Society from 1859 to 1891.

Samuel Ross Winans was a scholar in linguistics and Indology who studied at Princeton University. He later served Princeton as Professor of Greek and Instructor of Sanskrit (1876-1883) and as dean of the faculty (1899-1903).

Samuel Slater was an Indologist educated at King's College London. He held posts as Rector of St. Paul's School, Darjeeling (1850), Professor at Bishop's College, Calcutta (1850-1863), and Professor of Hindustani at King's College London (1861-1862).
